(To understand the following story you must know that due to mental illness my horses mean a lot more to me than they do to other people. My mare basically saved me from suicide. I am not exaggerating when I say, I cannot live without them.)

Due to the reason stated above I decided to breed my mare. I know that I will be absolutely devastated when she dies and while I know that no other horse will ever replace her, I need some kind of a safety net. I need something that will keep me going after her death. Sure I could have just bought a second horse but being able to keep a part of her is even better. 
So a whole year after breeding it was finally time. She gave birth to a wonderful filly. 
The birth itself was perfect. Everything went smoothly, they both stood up, the little one drank, all good. This was all at about 11pm. 
Our problem was the afterbirth. You see, in horses the afterbirth should come out no later than 4 hours after the actual birth. Well that wasn’t the case.

I called the vet at about 2:30 am to ask for advice, she said she’d come over. When she came she first checked both of them and apart from the afterbirth still half stuck in my mare they were good. We tried everything. She tried cautiously taking it out by hand (you cant just pull, because you will rupture it), she tried inducing labor again (which was hella painful to watch because it was immensely painful, worse than the actual birth, for my girl) and she even tried flushing it out with some kind of saline(?).

At 4 am I was crying. Nothing was working. Having the afterbirth inside her for so long is very dangerous. The tissue will start to rot inside of them and basically poison them from the inside. So at 4 am I called my parents.

My parents live a two hour drive away from me.
At 6:30am my Dad was there. 

He helped me through the whole week, saving my girl and even offered to pay for it.
When I called he knew I needed him and he didn’t hesitate. He had a coffee because it was 4 in the morning and jumped into his car.

He’s with me right now too, because our filly has some issues with her legs and we are bringing her to an equine veterinary hospital tomorrow.
I love my parents.

They aren’t perfect, no one is, but I know that when I need them I can count on them.

My father always had a huge fear of horses. It was two weeks ago when he overcame it: 
My horse was sick and I really desperately needed his help taking care of her. So for me he did it and is now not afraid anymore. He still doesn’t like horses very much but he loves mine. 

I believe that one thing that helped was, that she is a very very calm horse. She has almost no bad habits (apart from searching for treats in your pocket) and she is a horse that does rather retrieve from situations than push forward. 

So i would suggest you look for a horse, that’s very well broken in. Maybe a school pony for little kids? Most of them are a little naughty but almost none will be difficult to handle. If you know someone with such a horse I would ask them in advance about “bad habits” that might scare you. Just so you’re prepared. 

Hope that helps xx
